raw_recipe.headline: Fruit Salad
raw_recipe.description: Sour cream binds this salad of pineapple chunks, maraschino cherries, and mandarin orange slices with miniature marshmallows. Serve with a Thanksgiving dinner or as a dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Fruit Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Combine oranges, pineapple, marshmallows, sour cream, and cherries together in a large bowl. Chill and serve.

review.reviewBody: My dear mom passed down this recipe, it has been in our family many years and is almost identical to this. It is called Ambrosia Salad. It is my family's favorite. It calls for 1/4 c. shredded coconut(leave out if don't like), but it gives a nice flavor and sweetness to this, 1 c. sour cream or enough to moisten, 1 c. grapes halved, 1 c. mandarin oranges drained( I use more), 1 c. mini marshmellows and 1 c. crushed pineapple drained. Double for large crowds. You can basically add the fruits you like and mix with sour cream until your liking. I think the cherries is a great addition!We especially like this in the summer months but get cravings for it year round! My daughter begs me to make this all the time! This recipe is so close to this and that is why I gave it 5*. I think any way you make will be great! Thanks Tina for sharing!

Easy and tasty. Great taste and nice addition to a savory flavored meal. Almost desert like. I used fresh clementines, halved red grapes, added some juice from the cherries and threw in a couple of tablespoons of flaked coconut. Only a lone serving for leftovers, will make again. Easy to adjust recipe according to what you might have on hand. Will make again.

This brings me back to childhood! Love this recipe and agree-you can add whatever fruits you prefer. We used a can of mixed fruits,small can of mandarin oranges, small jar of maraschino cherries, small can of pineapple chunks, about a 1/4 c of flaked coconut and 8 oz sour cream (enough to moisten) like the idea of adding marshmallows before serving-will try this for Christmas. I usually make this for Easter dinner and I like to use the fruity kind of marshmallows for the pretty pastel colors! If people didnt know it was sour cream they couldnt tell. People have asked me why dont I just use cool-whip and I say that would make it unbearably sweet, sour cream is just right!!!

A friend made this at a birthday party and I ate it without knowing what was in it. I was shocked that the creaminess was from sour cream! She said she added all the ingredients except the marshmallows(add them before serving if you don't like mush) and let it set overnight to combine the flavors (and to take away the tang from the sour cream). I tried it at home and used fatfree sour cream with the same results. I also added a little of the cherry juice. Great recipe, Thanks!

My mother used to make this wonderful fruit salad that she called "5 Cup Fruit Salad" for every holiday and we all loved it. She recently passed away and I was trying to think of what all we use to put in it and I knew we used marshmellows, cherries, sour cream, canned pineapples and something else. I got on here to see if I could find one similar to hers. Back then they did not have mandarin (spelling?) oranges canned and I think (????) she used fresh oranges and possibly canned pears too. We would add cherry juice to the mixture for a colorful dish and would hold off on the marshmellows until it was about and hour before it was served otherwise it would become mushy. Sprinkly some chopped pecans or walnuts on top. Thank you so much for submitting this recipe so that I too can make this fabulous fruit salad that sound disgusting because of sour cream but is truly refreshing and oh so easy to make!

Pretty good! I made this for a friend who just had a baby. She has 3 young children, so I made this to entice the little ones. I halved the marshmallows. Next time I will only use 1/2 to 2/3 of the 16 oz container of sour cream instead of the whole thing.. I did use low fat sour cream, and it was delicious. No need to make this fattening. Next time I might add halved green grapes and coconut.

This is a family tradtion at our home with a few changes. I drain all my fruit the overnight and the next morning mix sour cream, marshmellows, pinapples, oranges and then I use a few cans of mixed fruit instead of the cherries then mix it all together. Then we take the fruit juice and make our family punch. My children come home every Holiday expecting it! Its a healthy and delicious receipe.

Yummo! Our family's new super fast throw together dessert. I just added fresh strawberries and bananas to make it more fresh tasting. Chilled for an hour to allow flavors to mix then served in wine glasses with few cut up strawberries to make a pretty presentation.

Delicious! My entire family (teens & adults) loved it.

Changes: I used fresh summer fruits--nectarines, bananas, red grapes, and fresh pineapple. I added a bag of sweetened coconut.

I have been eating this since I was a little girl. Recently I tried using Non-fat vanilla Greek yogurt instead of sour cream and it was amazing!!!! I think I'll stick with the yogurt-my family couldn't tell the difference and I knew I was sneaking some extra protein in a very yummy treat!!! Just an FYI I used about 1/2 of a large container of the yogurt, and I use crushed pineapple instead of chunks.
This was excellent! I made it the day before and only used 10 oz of Marshmallows. You could even use a lot less and it would still be wonderful!
Been in the family for 60 years! You can also add cool whip. You can add nuts and coconut if desired.
Same great recipe my mother made during Thanksgiving
Left the recipe as is!
My grandmother made this every year for Thanksgiving & Christmas. All of my siblings and cousins- and myself- loved it. For the maximum Grammy experience, it must be served in a red aluminum pot :)

My mom always made this for Thanksgiving and Christmas and always a top hit. She also added toasted coconut, but as another reviewer noted it’s not necessary if someone doesn’t like coconut. Easy to make, tastes wonderful and makes a great side dish or salad.
I don't have the recipe yet.
For our three college grads, grands. I think they are going to love it... we shall see
I love this recipe! I will totally make it again!!!!
